name: Meter Passport BSC handler credits untransferred wrapped-native deposits
summary: Meter's ChainBridge fork added a wrapped-native path to ERC20Handler.deposit(bytes32,uint8,uint64,address,bytes) that skips the token movement entirely for the configured wtoken: `// ether case, the weth already in handler, do nothing` guards `if (tokenAddress != _wtokenAddress) { burnERC20 | lockERC20 }`. That assumption only holds for Bridge.depositETH, which requires `amount == msg.value - fee` and wraps the value itself. Bridge.deposit stayed callable for the same resourceID and requires only `msg.value == fee`, so any caller could write a DepositRecord and emit Deposit for an arbitrary WBNB amount without transferring anything, and the relayer set released or minted that amount on the destination chain.
notes: ERC20Handler is a non-upgradeable contract created directly by an EOA. Its runtime hashes to 0x051166e9379a6663dc05e5fd97aec94411bd05cb1aeea836046d12df2b02efa3 both at the deployment block 7848927 and at block 14992189 immediately before the exploit, so the defect-bearing bytecode is unchanged over the whole interval.

BSC leg, two components caused by BSC-executed deposits. (1) The anchor deposit credited 3632.795971816270126503 WBNB without transferring anything; 39 seconds later the relayer set executed the matching proposal on BSC itself (destinationChainID 4 is BSC's own Passport id) and ERC20Handler 0x5945241bbb68b4454bb67bd2b069e74c09ac3d51 sent exactly 3632795971816270126503 wei of native BNB to the attacker in 0xf70b4aa715c0a04079c56cd9036cc63cdb6101e400520a8f2c019ad2ced5358e, an exact depletion of the handler's wrapped-native reserve, valued at the WBNB observation nearest the anchor. (2) Two further BSC deposits of 15000 WBNB each to destinationChainID 5 (Moonriver) minted 30000 unbacked BNB.bsc to the attacker on Moonriver, which he sold into the single SushiSwap BNB.bsc/ETH pair over six swaps for exactly 338.181429214488085156 ETH. Those sales moved BNB.bsc from a 422.88 USD spot mark to a realised 34.35 USD per token, so that component uses realised-proceeds while the aggregate remains other. Spot-marking 30000 BNB would imply 12.7M USD at a price at which the position could not be sold. Counted in the Ethereum leg below rather than here: 398850.18169558374 BUSD that the same BSC handler released to the attacker in 0xe045c40c51250ef611f06c4f11ab4ea11486cd8f6827ed03eb06ad4c8c6cf53e and 0x3fb520c6b44dcbf18fcd75757883a158e6b075420225e01b6761b6a2645157eb, because those proposals originate from the Ethereum deposit routed through Passport chain 3. Excluded from this record: Hundred Finance's roughly 3.3M USD of knock-on borrowing losses, which are a third party's oracle exposure to the crashed Moonriver BNB price. Ethereum leg of the same campaign (WETH, WBTC and BUSD components): Two Ethereum-executed Bridge.deposit calls exercised the defect and their consequences are disjoint from the BSC components above. (1) The anchor credited 422508708639363167140 wei of WETH to Passport destination chain 1, which is Ethereum's own Passport id, so the relayer set executed the matching proposal on Ethereum 53 blocks later and handler 0xde4fc7c3c5e7be3f16506fcc790a8d93f8ca0b40 unwrapped and sent exactly 422508708639363167140 wei of native ETH to the attacker in 0xd619ace8a8cca2f7eb72dbc0a896fc2d4d8b20aa11f4d747f1a5333305bbb875. That amount equals the handler's entire WETH balance at block 14146529, which fell to zero; the component is valued at the WETH observation nearest the anchor. (2) The second deposit credited 1500 WETH to Passport chain 3, which is Meter mainnet (eip155:82), and minted 1500 unbacked WETH.eth 0x79a61d3a28f8c8537a3df63092927cfa1150fb3c to the attacker there. He sold all 1500 on Meter: 992 into the BUSD.bsc pair 0xe81171e3e984285caf2e2a89ffedb92f4e424125 for 398850.181695583747921848 BUSD.bsc and 508 into the WBTC.eth pair 0x3d0ca02704d45ba2966c0be7a4f3c6cd4163569e for 2.74068396 WBTC.eth, then burned both back out of Passport, so the Ethereum handler released 2.74068396 WBTC in 0x519a6630d377d89d57a49bedeffc5606c1089c9844bfc3d10ddc230a41a52b4d and the BSC handler released 398850.181695583747921848 BUSD in the two chain-3 proposals that the BSC leg leaves uncounted. Those realised proceeds are used rather than a spot mark on 1500 WETH, because the attacker's own selling collapsed WETH.eth on Meter from about 3022 USD to a realised 341.76 USD per token and 1500 WETH could not have been sold at spot; the aggregate method is therefore "other". Excluded from this record: 630.829743049062048095 ETH that Celer cBridge 0x5427fefa711eff984124bfbb1ab6fbf5e3da1820 relayed to the attacker on Ethereum in four transfers between blocks 14146848 and 14146967, because their PbBridge.Relay payloads carry srcChainId 56 and they move the BSC leg's proceeds, which the WBNB component already counts; and the 0.966647 ETH the attacker was funded with before the campaign.

The 30000 BNB.bsc component is realised on Moonriver (eip155:1285), which the onchain verifier is not wired for; its quantities were reproduced through the Etherscan v2 Moonriver endpoint rather than by scripts/verify.mjs.

The Meter mainnet leg (eip155:82) that turned the second deposit's 1500 unbacked WETH.eth into the BUSD and WBTC components is outside the chains scripts/verify.mjs is wired for; its mint, sale and burn quantities were reproduced with eth_getLogs against rpc.meter.io and are cited in the review note rather than as a structured onchain source.

The same attacker exercised the byte-identical Ethereum deployment of ERC20Handler (0xde4fc7c3c5e7be3f16506fcc790a8d93f8ca0b40, Bridge 0xa2a22b46b8df38cd7c55e6bf32ea5a32637cf2b1) minutes later through deposits 0x2d3987963b77159cfe4f820532d729b0364c7f05511f23547765c75b110b629c and 0xdfea6413c7eb3068093dcbbe65bcc9ba635e227c35e57fe482bb5923c89e31f7. That leg is merged here as the WETH, WBTC and BUSD components; the code age is measured on the BSC anchor.
